title: Create a Pull Request
description: Share your work for review — the way code gets into production on every real team.

steps.instruction: Create a new branch: `git checkout -b my-first-pr`
hints: Branch names usually describe the change, e.g. `fix-login-bug` or `add-dark-mode`
Don't commit directly to main — always work on a branch

steps.instruction: Make a small change, then stage and commit it
hints: Keep the change small — it's easier to review

steps.instruction: Push your branch to GitHub: `git push -u origin my-first-pr`
hints: The -u flag sets the upstream so future `git push`es don't need the branch name
The output will include a link to open a PR — keep it handy

steps.instruction: Open the PR on GitHub and fill in a clear title and description
hints: Follow the link git printed, or go to your repo on GitHub and click 'Compare & pull request'
Describe: what it does, why, how to test. Add screenshots if UI changed.
Request a reviewer if your team expects one
